A fixture sequence is not a production transition graph or an MQTT ordering guarantee. One bounded local end-to-end run, not maximum capacity or SLO validation.

serviceRuns.limitation: Synthetic CMS-shaped service IDs/API keys and simulated creates; no call to messages-app/services-func CreateMessages, Services CMS, real IO queues/change feeds or Azure. A fixture sequence is not a production transition graph or an MQTT ordering guarantee. One bounded local end-to-end run, not maximum capacity or SLO validation.

serviceRuns.pipeline: Service onboarding -> one public topic; simulated creates -> correlated events -> AMQP TLS confirmed ingress -> real publisher worker -> MQTT TLS QoS1 consumer

serviceRuns.limitation: Synthetic CMS-shaped service IDs/API keys and simulated creates; no call to messages-app/services-func CreateMessages, Services CMS, real IO queues/change feeds or Azure. A fixture sequence is not a production transition graph or an MQTT ordering guarantee. One bounded local end-to-end run, not maximum capacity or SLO validation.

serviceRuns.pipeline: Service onboarding -> one public topic; simulated creates -> correlated events -> AMQP TLS confirmed ingress -> real publisher worker -> MQTT TLS QoS1 consumer

serviceRuns.limitation: Synthetic CMS-shaped service IDs/API keys and simulated creates; no call to messages-app/services-func CreateMessages, Services CMS, real IO queues/change feeds or Azure. A fixture sequence is not a production transition graph or an MQTT ordering guarantee. One bounded local end-to-end run, not maximum capacity or SLO validation.
serviceRuns.pipeline: Service onboarding -> one public topic; simulated creates -> correlated events -> AMQP TLS confirmed ingress -> real publisher worker -> MQTT TLS QoS1 consumer
